author: h. w. champion
title: Josh Gottheimer criticizes spending and NYC policies in recent tweets
text:
U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer, who represents New Jersey’s 5th district, addressed several issues in a series of tweets posted on June 16 and 17, 2026.
On June 16, Gottheimer criticized the financial management of a local construction project: “Insane! This so called ‘privately funded’ ballroom is now more than $200M over budget, and taxpayers are footing half the bill. That’s unacceptable. Jersey families are already struggling with the rising costs of everyday life. Their taxes shouldn’t go to Trump’s vanity project” . The tweet highlights concerns about public funding being used for what he describes as an unnecessary expense amid broader economic pressures faced by residents.
Later that day, Gottheimer raised concerns about New York City’s bus idling tax and its impact on transit operations: “A bus needs its engine running to power the battery to lower a wheelchair lift, run the A/C, and complete a required safety check. But NYC’s bus idling tax is fining our hard-working drivers for basic safety operations — putting seniors and disabled passengers at risk.” He argued that the current policy penalizes drivers performing essential duties necessary for passenger safety.
On June 17, Gottheimer issued a brief statement regarding security threats, “My statement on the planned attack targeting the White House and pro-Israel Members of Congress: https://t.co/E6YzHSLtd2” .
Gottheimer has served in Congress since 2017 after defeating Scott Garrett. Born in Livingston, New Jersey in 1975, he currently resides in Wyckoff. He holds degrees from both the University of Pennsylvania (BA) and Harvard University (JD).
